Same rules as competitors.yaml: the vendor's own published list price, in USD, per year, on annual billing where they offer it, with the page it came from. Every price here is also on the site, and scripts/pricing-calculator.test.cjs fails if one disagrees with the ladder in competitors.yaml.

steps: [pageviews a month, USD a year] from the smallest plan up. A third item, "gap", means the vendor sells steps between this one and the one before that the site hasn't checked, so traffic in between is shown as a range, never an estimate.

above: what happens past the last step. talk = ask us, sales = the vendor quotes it, cap = the plan stops there, overage = overagePerEvent a month past the last step, unpublished = no price on the site.

sites and team: null means unlimited. team counts people besides the account owner, which is how Plausible's Starter plan reads (one site, no team members). "unpublished" means the vendor doesn't say.
funnels and revenue: true, false, or {fits, note} where the answer needs a sentence.

plans.note: Unlimited sites and teammates. Funnels and revenue are included.
plans.aboveNote: We don't publish a price past a million pageviews and custom events a month. Email sales@feasible.lol and we'll price the extra volume.

beyond.note: Past 10 sites or 10 team members it's their Enterprise plan, which is priced by quote.
Extra sites come in packs of 50, up to 15 packs. Past that you have to ask them.

funnels.note: Their goals can have several steps, and their docs call that a funnel.

revenue.note: We couldn't find revenue tracking on their pricing page or in their goals docs.
